title: 41. Numeracy & Number Systems: Decimal Multiplication
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply two decimals with one decimal place each.
questions.question: What is \(0.6\times 0.3\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits without the decimal points: \(6\times 3=18\). Each factor has one decimal place, so the product has \(1+1=2\) decimal places. Therefore, \(0.6\times 0.3=0.18\). The correct answer is \(0.18\).
questions.hint: Multiply the digits first, then count the total number of decimal places in the factors.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a decimal with one decimal place by a decimal with one decimal place.
questions.question: What is \(1.2\times 0.5\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits: \(12\times 5=60\). The factors \(1.2\) and \(0.5\) each have one decimal place, so the product has \(1+1=2\) decimal places. Therefore, \(1.2\times 0.5=0.60=0.6\). The correct answer is \(0.6\).
questions.hint: After multiplying, place the decimal point two places from the right and remove any trailing zero.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a decimal with one decimal place by a whole number.
questions.question: What is \(2.5\times 4\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits: \(25\times 4=100\). The factor \(2.5\) has one decimal place, so the product is \(10.0=10\). Therefore, \(2.5\times 4=10\). The correct answer is \(10\).
questions.hint: Count the decimal places in the factor, then simplify the product if possible.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a decimal with one decimal place by a decimal with one decimal place.
questions.question: What is \(3.7\times 0.2\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits: \(37\times 2=74\). The factors \(3.7\) and \(0.2\) each have one decimal place, so the product has \(1+1=2\) decimal places. Therefore, \(3.7\times 0.2=0.74\). The correct answer is \(0.74\).
questions.hint: Multiply as whole numbers, then place the decimal point two places from the right.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a decimal with one decimal place by a decimal with one decimal place.
questions.question: What is \(6.4\times 1.5\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits: \(64\times 15=960\). The factors \(6.4\) and \(1.5\) each have one decimal place, so the product has \(1+1=2\) decimal places. Therefore, \(6.4\times 1.5=9.60=9.6\). The correct answer is \(9.6\).
questions.hint: Multiply without decimal points, then count the total decimal places in the factors.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a decimal with two decimal places by a whole number.
questions.question: What is \(0.75\times 8\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits: \(75\times 8=600\). The factor \(0.75\) has two decimal places, so the product is \(6.00=6\). Therefore, \(0.75\times 8=6\). The correct answer is \(6\).
questions.hint: Count two decimal places in the product, then remove trailing zeros.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a decimal with one decimal place by a decimal with one decimal place.
questions.question: What is \(12.5\times 0.4\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits: \(125\times 4=500\). The factors \(12.5\) and \(0.4\) each have one decimal place, so the product has \(1+1=2\) decimal places. Therefore, \(12.5\times 0.4=5.00=5\). The correct answer is \(5\).
questions.hint: After multiplying, place the decimal point two places from the right and simplify.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a decimal with three decimal places by a decimal with one decimal place.
questions.question: What is \(0.125\times 0.8\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits: \(125\times 8=1000\). The factor \(0.125\) has three decimal places and \(0.8\) has one decimal place, so the product has \(3+1=4\) decimal places. Therefore, \(0.125\times 0.8=0.1000=0.1\). The correct answer is \(0.1\).
questions.hint: Count all decimal places in the factors, then simplify the product.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a decimal with one decimal place by a decimal with one decimal place.
questions.question: What is \(4.5\times 2.4\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits: \(45\times 24=1080\). The factors \(4.5\) and \(2.4\) each have one decimal place, so the product has \(1+1=2\) decimal places. Therefore, \(4.5\times 2.4=10.80=10.8\). The correct answer is \(10.8\).
questions.hint: Multiply as whole numbers, then place the decimal point two places from the right.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply two decimals each with two decimal places.
questions.question: What is \(0.06\times 0.07\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the digits: \(6\times 7=42\). The factors \(0.06\) and \(0.07\) each have two decimal places, so the product has \(2+2=4\) decimal places. Therefore, \(0.06\times 0.07=0.0042\). The correct answer is \(0.0042\).
questions.hint: Count all decimal places in the two factors before placing the decimal point.
